correctness.rationale: Exact zero-sum ℓ1 polytope identity; exposed root vertices; strict one-sided derivative a_i+b_j>T; every illuminated directed-edge set is an intersecting bipartite graph and hence a star of at most m−1 arcs. The sum of root-vertex coverage inequalities gives I*≥m, and explicit m outgoing-star directions cover all boundary faces. Equality in the two sharp inequalities forces only full stars with exact per-root mass one, and the system alpha_i+beta_j=1 has exactly alpha_i=theta, beta_j=1−theta for m≥3; only theta=0 and theta=1 are possible for m unit-weight directions. Recomputed explicit small-dimension exact tests from the standalone file, without treating them as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Determines exact ordinary and fractional illumination for all simplex difference bodies in unbounded dimension and rigidly classifies all optimal finite fractional vertex-incidence configurations as a one-dimensional segment with exactly two integral vertices. This sharpened structural result explains the geometry of optimal illumination at every root, beyond a special-case computation or a repeated general upper bound. It is motivated by newly established sharp universal fractional bounds and the natural simplex difference body.
